c.tagline: Beaches, nightlife, and endless tropical energy.

taxi.color: Blue songthaews (baht buses); metered taxis rare

emergency.note: Tourist Police on 1155 have English-speaking operators; 191 call-takers often do not speak English.

hood_landmark.Central Pattaya: Beach Road promenade and the Central Pattaya (Central Festival) beachfront mall
hood_landmark.North Pattaya: Terminal 21 Pattaya mall by the Dolphin Roundabout
hood_landmark.Jomtien Beach: Jomtien's long, calmer sandy beach and night market
hood_landmark.Naklua: The Sanctuary of Truth, a giant hand-carved wooden temple

avoid.reason: On and around Walking Street watch for bar-bill scams, drink spiking and pickpockets, and beware jet-ski damage scams on the beach.

hood_desc: Central Pattaya is the busy tourist heart, packed with big shopping malls like Central Festival, Beach Road, hotels and restaurants, it suits first-time visitors who want everything walkable and lively.
North Pattaya is calmer and a bit more upscale and residential while still close to the action, appealing to travelers and long-stay expats who want quiet nights but easy access to the center.
South Pattaya is the most intense party zone, home to Walking Street with its bars, clubs and go-go venues plus budget guesthouses, best for nightlife seekers and younger, price-conscious travelers.
Jomtien Beach is a longer, more relaxed stretch of sand with a laid-back mix of families, watersports and a large expat and long-stay community, ideal for those wanting beach time without the chaos.

Naklua keeps a traditional Thai fishing-village feel with fresh seafood markets and the quieter Wong Amat beach nearby, suiting families, retirees and long-stay visitors seeking a more local, peaceful base.

water.note: Avoid tap water; use bottled or filtered water, and check that ice is made from purified water.

transit.pay: Songthaews (shared pickup-truck 'baht buses') cost a flat 10-20 baht (~US$0.30-0.60) on their loop routes - hop on, ring the bell, and pay the driver cash when you get off. Chartering one privately or going off-route costs more, so agree on the price first. Grab and Bolt apps work well for cars and motorbike taxis.
transit.hours: Baht buses circulate on Beach Road and Second Road from early morning until around midnight, more frequently than any schedule - just flag one down.
transit.note: No formal transit system - locals and tourists get around by baht bus, motorbike taxi, and Grab/Bolt rideshare; Bangkok is reachable by intercity bus or the airport highway.

transit.m: Suvarnabhumi Burapha airport bus to Pattaya (~1 hr)

food.name: Hoi jor
food.desc: Chonburi coastal classic: crab and minced pork wrapped in bean-curd skin, deep-fried to a crisp roll and dipped in sweet plum sauce.

places.name: Nong Mon Market
places.note: Chonburi's landmark food market; several long-running hoi jor vendors fry them fresh all day.

places.name: Ang Sila Market
places.note: Old fishing-town market where the crab comes off the boats a few metres away.

food.name: Khao lam
food.desc: Sweet coconut sticky rice roasted inside a bamboo tube, split open at the table. Bang Saen is the dish's most famous home in Thailand.

places.name: Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand for its bamboo sticky rice, with black bean, taro and custard fillings.

places.name: Nong Mon Market
places.note: Rows of khao lam stalls; buy warm from the roasting fire and eat on the beach.

food.name: Pu nim and steamed blue crab
food.desc: Chonburi blue crab steamed whole or soft-shell crab fried with garlic and pepper, the province's best-known seafood.

places.name: Mum Aroi
places.note: Seaside restaurant among old fishing boats; a locals-and-expats favourite for crab.

places.name: Lung Sawai Seafood
places.note: Thirty-plus years on the beach road; steamed crab and crab stir-fried in curry powder.

food.name: Hoi tod
food.desc: Crispy-chewy mussel or oyster pancake fried in a batter with egg and bean sprouts, served with sriracha-style chilli sauce.

places.name: Thepprasit Night Market
places.note: Huge Friday-to-Sunday market with hoi tod griddles going all evening.

places.name: Lan Pho Park food stalls
places.note: Evening seafood stalls beside the park, cheaper and far more local than the beach road.

food.name: Ho mok talay
food.desc: Seafood and red curry steamed into a soft savoury custard in a banana-leaf cup, a Nong Mon market signature.

places.name: Nong Mon Market
places.note: The market is best known for ho mok alongside khao lam and kanom chak.

places.name: Ang Sila Market
places.note: Fish-market stalls steam it to order using the morning's catch.

food.name: Kaeng som pla
food.desc: Fiery sour orange curry with fish, tamarind and vegetables. Punchier and sourer than anything on the tourist menus.

places.name: Lung Sawai Seafood
places.note: Known for its sour orange curry with fish roe, a house speciality for decades.

places.name: Krua Laew Tae R-Rom
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand; a short daily menu built entirely on that morning's catch.

food.name: Cha yen
food.desc: Thai iced tea: strong spiced black tea poured over ice and swirled with condensed and evaporated milk into its trademark orange.

places.name: Thepprasit Night Market
places.note: Dozens of tea carts pulling cha yen to order; among the cheapest in the city.

places.name: Nong Mon Market
places.note: Old-school stalls that still brew the tea in cloth socks rather than from powder.

food.name: Draught Thai lager
food.desc: Ice-cold Chang or Singha on tap, poured over ice in the Thai way, and the standard partner to a table of grilled seafood.

places.name: Lan Pho Park seafood stalls
places.note: Beer buckets and plastic stools facing the water, where Pattaya locals actually drink.

places.name: Bali Hai Pier beer terraces
places.note: Sunset draught with a view over the bay and the ferry boats to Koh Larn.

landmarks: Sanctuary of Truth

This monumental all-wood temple, still under construction after decades, is carved entirely with intricate Buddhist and Hindu mythology and set dramatically on the seafront. Its soaring spires and craftsmanship make it one of Thailand's most extraordinary structures.
Big Buddha Hill (Wat Phra Yai)

A massive golden Buddha statue crowns this hilltop temple, offering sweeping views over Pattaya Bay along with the ringing of hundreds of prayer bells. It's a peaceful, spiritual counterpoint to the city's neon energy.
Pattaya Viewpoint (Pratamnak Hill)
This scenic overlook delivers the classic postcard shot of Pattaya's curving coastline and turquoise bay. It's especially stunning at sunset when the sky and sea both glow gold.
Walking Street

Pattaya's legendary nightlife strip comes alive after dark with neon lights, bars, and nonstop energy along the beachfront. Love it or hate it, it's an essential slice of the city's after-dark identity.
Nong Nooch Tropical Garden

This sprawling botanical park blends manicured French-style gardens, cactus fields, and cultural dance shows featuring elephants and traditional Thai performances. It's a colorful, family-friendly day trip from the city center.
Wat Yansangwararam

This tranquil temple complex mixes Thai, Chinese, and Cambodian architectural styles around a peaceful lake, offering a serene escape from Pattaya's bustle. Its varied pavilions and pagodas reward slow exploration.
Pattaya Floating Market

Wooden boats piled with produce and street food drift through canals lined with stilted shops representing Thailand's four regions. It's a lively, photogenic dive into traditional Thai market culture.
Art in Paradise Pattaya

This interactive 3D art museum turns visitors into part of the painting, with playful optical-illusion murals covering every wall, floor, and ceiling. It's one of the most Instagrammed attractions in the city.
Mini Siam

Wander among miniature replicas of Thailand's and the world's most famous landmarks, from Angkor Wat to the Eiffel Tower, all scaled down within one park. It's a whimsical, photo-friendly world tour in miniature.
Underwater World Pattaya
An aquarium near central Pattaya with a 105-meter acrylic tunnel letting visitors walk beneath sharks, rays, and thousands of reef fish.

train.note: Pattaya has only a small station on SRT's eastern line with a slow ordinary train to/from Bangkok on weekdays plus weekend excursion services - no international trains. Most travelers take the bus; Thailand's cross-border trains (to Laos and Malaysia) leave from Bangkok.

bus.note: No direct international coaches from Pattaya. Roong Reuang Coach (https://pattayabus.com/) runs frequent buses to Bangkok's Ekkamai and Mo Chit terminals and Suvarnabhumi Airport; Transport Co. (https://www.transport.co.th/) covers other domestic routes from the North Pattaya terminal.

ferry.note: No international ferries. Cheap passenger boats to Koh Larn island leave Bali Hai Pier roughly hourly through the day; the cross-gulf Pattaya-Hua Hin fast ferry has been suspended for several years.

half.name: Koh Larn
half.blurb: Nearby island escape with clear waters, white-sand beaches, snorkeling and easygoing seaside viewpoints.

half.name: Nong Nooch Tropical Botanical Garden
half.blurb: Sprawling landscaped gardens with topiary, orchids, cultural shows and a photogenic French-style formal garden.

half.name: Koh Si Chang
half.blurb: Quiet island of temples, a former royal palace and rocky coves reached via Si Racha.

half.name: Khao Kheow Open Zoo
half.blurb: Expansive open-range zoo where animals roam wooded hillsides, home to celebrity pygmy hippo Moo Deng.

half.name: Koh Samet
half.blurb: Popular national-park island fringed with powdery white beaches and calm, brilliantly clear swimming water.

full.name: Ayutthaya
full.blurb: Ancient royal capital scattered with crumbling temples, brick prangs and the iconic Buddha head in tree roots.
